checks.note: onBookingCancelledByParent (RefundEnqueueListener.java:46-50) does enqueue a restore on only sessionPackPurchaseId != null && isRefundEligible(), but whether that over-credits depends on when pack sessions are deducted: the finding assumes deduction at settlement, while the diff's own comment ("else: forfeited (<=24h) — session consumed", line 51) implies deduction at booking time. BookingCancelledByParentEvent's refundEligible construction and the pack-deduction site in CancellationRefundService/booking code are not shown, so this cannot be settled from the diff.

The new guard in deductSession (purchase.getPausedUntil().isAfter(Instant.now()) throwing payment.packPaused) is unconditional and takes no booking/session-date input, so the mechanism is real; but the trigger depends on pausePack leaving an ACCEPTED booking uncancelled and on the settlement path recording a failure, and neither pausePack nor the caller is in the shown diff.

The watch(selected) handler nulls attemptKey unconditionally and the catch in confirmPurchase only clears the key when e?.response exists, so the described loss-then-new-key mechanism exists in the script; but whether `selected` can actually change while `purchasing` is true depends on the template (e.g., the pack selector being disabled during purchase), which is outside the shown diff.

No reported finding addresses the lack of a per-booking refund marker or double-crediting on event redelivery.

R3 pins the exact defect: attemptKey reset whenever e.response exists, so a 5xx/timeout after capture leads to a retry with a fresh key and a second charge; R4 describes the same key-discard defect triggered via a concurrent-submit Stripe idempotency conflict.
